stats.name: Health

stats.name: Size

surcharge.formula: upgrade number n (counting all prior upgrades on the model) costs list price for n <= freeUpgrades, else list price + (n - 1)

Resistances, vulnerabilities and size are what make a creature a creature rather than a min-maxed fighter, so they no longer count toward the upgrade number. Stat stacking is still taxed exactly as before.
surcharge.healthStepNote: one 2-Health step counts as one upgrade

traits.name: Extra arms
traits.desc: +2 hands per purchase (max two purchases: 4 or 6 arms). Extra hands carry more gear (e.g. a Heavy melee weapon and a Shield). Flurry is built in: if it carries 2 or more melee weapons, its melee Attack makes one attack with each, all stepped down, up to 3 attacks with four arms or 4 with six. This replaces Rapid for that Attack and still counts as its one Attack action. Its Flurry attacks may be split between any enemies it is Engaged with (declared before the throw). Each extra pair of arms cancels one Outnumber step for enemies attacking it (six arms: none; a Swarm squad keeps its third step).
traits.verified: new in 0.10.2 (Extra arms and Flurry merged); 12 per pair is a guess; 0.10.4 added split attacks and Outnumber cancelling - likely worth more than 12

weaponMods.desc: On a Critical, the target loses its next action.

weaponMods.name: Force
weaponMods.desc: On a hit, push the target 5 cm directly away.

weaponModRules.appliesTo: one weapon on one model; buy it again for another weapon
weaponModRules.stacking: a weapon may carry several different effects (e.g. Acid + Toxic + Fire) but never the same one twice; each is paid separately
weaponModRules.cost: added to the weapon's cost; gear, so never surcharged
weaponModRules.pricing: round 8: fitted against the 15-weapon list (damage ~4.2/pt, range ~0.7/10cm, rms 0.89). Effects below the harness's 8-point resolution, so priced by that fit rather than measured in battle.
weaponModRules.squads: paid per model, like the weapon itself
weaponModRules.multiHit: effects apply per hit, but conditions do not stack (see conditionRules), so extra copies across several weapons add little against one target; the main risk is spreading them across many targets (Blast, squads)

vulnerabilityRefundCap.rule: refunds from Vulnerable traits can never exceed what the model spends on resistances, Burning aura, Regenerate and weapon effects of other elements; a weakness offsets a nature, it is not free points
vulnerabilityRefundCap.why: otherwise a player takes Vulnerable to an element nobody at the table uses and banks the refund

elementsNote: arcane has no resistance, weakness or weapon effect yet; reserved for powers

flaws.desc: Drawbacks any character can take for points back. A starting scar is a flaw with backstory.

refundCap.rule: per model; weakness refunds are capped separately (vulnerabilityRefundCap)
refundCap.squads: a squad flaw applies to every model and refunds per model

flaws.mustBite: every flaw must matter in ordinary play; the simulator flags any flaw that changes win rate by less than its refund
flaws.surcharge: flaws are downgrades, so they never count toward the surcharge

list.name: Coward
list.desc: Will tests step down when no friend is within 10 cm.

list.name: Hothead
list.desc: At the start of its activation, if an enemy is within 15 cm and it is not Engaged, it must Charge that enemy unless it passes a Will test.

list.name: Slow reflexes
list.desc: Never gains a Ready token, so it can never react.

list.name: Clumsy
list.desc: Interact tests step down; a failed climb or jump test means it falls.

list.name: Short-sighted
list.desc: No long shots; ranged attacks beyond 30 cm step down.

list.name: Loner
list.desc: Friendly murmurs and reckonings do not affect it, and it never counts toward Outnumber.

list.name: Bloodthirsty
list.desc: If a Down enemy is in contact, its Attack must Finish that enemy.

list.name: Unlucky
list.desc: Its side cannot spend Nerve on its rolls.

list.name: Greedy
list.desc: Campaign: takes 2 Cash from the band after every battle it fights in, or leaves.

list.name: Wanted
list.desc: Campaign: the scenario AI may add a bounty hunter aimed at this model (paid from the scenario budget).

startingScars.desc: A recruit may start with one scar from Fate rows 3-8 as a flaw. It can be Mended or Replaced at camp like any other scar, and feeds the epithet prompt from the start.
startingScars.note: refund replaces the normal stat-downgrade refund for that scar; counts toward the flaw cap

hands.rule: Each model has hands (default 2). Weapons and a Shield need hands to be carried: one each, two for Two-handed. A model may carry any gear its hands allow, but still makes one Attack action per activation.
hands.noHands: a model with 0 hands (a worm, a turret) uses only natural weapons reskinned as Light or Unarmed, and cannot Interact that needs handling, unless given Tools

conditionRules.stacking: conditions never stack: a model is either Burning/Tainted/Pinned or not. Applying a condition it already has only restarts its duration.
conditionRules.acid: Acid armour step-down does not stack
